speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; please tell me, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. The combination of wrist pain, fever, and your recent camping trip in Minnesota is concerning for a tick-borne infection like Lyme disease or Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever. You mentioned a self-resolving knee pain last week; was this joint swollen or red? Also, please describe the appearance and location of the skin lesions you have.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of painful violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists and hands, combined with acute monoarthritis of the left wrist and a recent camping trip, is highly suggestive of early syphilis or Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever. Were these lesions present before the wrist pain began, and do you have any other lesions on your body or a fever history beyond the chills? REQUEST TEST: RPR, VDRL. REQUEST IMAGES: Skin Lesions.

speaker: Doctor
text: The recent measurement readings are normal and do not contradict your clinical presentation. To further differentiate between the suspected tick-borne illnesses and syphilis, have you noticed any rash on your trunk or other parts of your body besides the hands and wrists?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever (RMSF)

The combination of a camping trip in Minnesota, monoarthritis of the wrist, chills, and violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the extremities is classic for early RMSF. Do you have a history of tick bites, and have you noticed any rash spreading to your palms, soles, or trunk? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_Full_Body_Scan.
